tagline: The old salt traders' pass, still carrying freight.
intro: NM 47 comes down from Rio Communities, across the Rio Grande from Belen, to meet US 60, and the highway turns east into Abo Pass, between the Manzano Mountains to the north and the Los Pinos Mountains to the south, toward the ruins at Abo.

It is an old way through. Traders between the Rio Grande pueblos and the plains carried salt, beans, cotton and buffalo meat over it, and the Spanish used it to reach their salt missions. The Santa Fe Railway put its freight line through the canyon because the grade held to 1.25 percent, against 3.5 on Raton Pass. Passenger trains quit the canyon in 1971. The freight did not.

moments.title: Abo Canyon
moments.text: US 60 shares the 5,771-foot pass with the railroad, where in 2006 almost 90 trains a day came through, most of them more than a mile long.

moments.title: Abo
moments.text: A small railroad town that was empty by 1940, though in 1933 a posse of more than 200 men still could not find one fugitive in its arroyos and badlands.

moments.title: Abo Pueblo
moments.text: The pueblo stood by a cluster of springs on the east slope of the pass, and the ruins of its mission church of San Gregorio belong to Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument.
